build: Software Projects disk, alternate D64 with LA–LJ files

exclude: Disk staging for bytes copied to $1E00 and graphics decoded to $4000; disk tail remains in the queue.
extra: Scene bytes copied by the runtime loader
Tail of the file loaded at $8010, role unresolved

comments.text: The first copied byte in the scene record is $01. The caller starts executing one byte later.

Save and reload the caller stack pointer, install the shared raster handler and configure the hallway colours. Convert screen cells at $4000 through the colour table at $7700, copy the digit glyphs, select character mode pointers and initialize sprites.

Restore the saved stack, initialize the background colours and select VIC bank $4000 and character matrix $4000. Refresh colour RAM from lookup page $77 and copy the score glyphs before setting up the sprites.
Copy the 90-byte table at $3200 to $44–$9D with X counting down from $59.
Wait for two CIA2 timer periods, then update the hallway. If $2D23 is set, enable all eight sprites. Dispatch the $2D25 path or poll the action routines beginning at $274A.
Start a 25-pass transition countdown. At count $11 call $2ABA with A=5, and call $28B8 on each pass.
Use A to choose the six coordinate bytes and three frame pointers for sprites 1–3. Merge the selected expansion mask before installing the positions and frame pointers.
Use A to select sprite 0 coordinates, expansion bits and a packed source. Select pointer $A9 and build its 64-byte image at $6A40 from a zero count and trailing literals.
Enable the selected sprites, draw the three-row room patch from selector 2, and expand sprites 1 and 2 in both directions before placing the next pose.
Select pose 5, wait ten periods and reset the sprite positions. Subtract $14 from five sprite Y coordinates and let the next approach advance while checking input and its timing flags.
Install $2CA3 as raster target, configure the upper four sprites and time a 25-pass animation. Switch the table selector when the counter reaches $11.
Clear sprite high X, set colours for sprites 1–3 and select their graphics and initial positions. The next input window starts after the delay at $2291.
Poll for changed joystick input on each of six timer periods. An exact fire mask takes the animation at $2308. Timeout changes the sprite set and jumps to the failure delay at $2713.
Set the mirror flag and load pointers $63 and $5E through the sprite transformation routine. Place the sprites from the table at $2E41.
Check six timer periods for the same fire mask as the first jump window. Valid input branches to $245B. Otherwise install the missed-jump position and pose before the failure delay.
Update the moving sprites each period and accept a new exact joystick mask $02 within the seven-period window. The timeout path uses the coordinate table at $3197.
Update the moving sprites and look for a change to the exact right mask $08 within ten timer periods. If the counter expires use the coordinate table at $319F and go to $2713.
Load the delay count $28 and call the wait at $27F9 before showing the failure interstitial.

Show the resident failure interstitial at $0ECD and jump to the scene restart at $1E04. The adjacent entry at $271E runs a separate overlay sequence before returning to the caller with the outcome decremented.
Write $FF to CIA1 port A, invert the joystick sample and compare it with the previous active-high sample. Retain the new sample at $28.
For Y iterations, increase three Y coordinates in each of six zero-page sprite pose groups.
Call the sprite updater at $277B for indices 3 through 0, using $0D to hold the index.
Use the slot in $0D to locate its divider and frame pointer. On expiry reload the divider to two, update the sprite frame and apply the slot's vertical step.
Wait A times using the resident two-period timer routine. Read the joystick between waits.
For A iterations wait, sample the joystick and step the four moving sprites through $276F.
Wait and sample the joystick A times, calling the periodic encounter update at $28B8.
Wait and read the joystick A times. Call $29AE between waits to advance the pair of animated sprites.
Use A to choose the source and screen destination words, X for row count and Y for width. Write companion colour 1 for each cell and advance both destination pointers by 40 between rows.
Write four blank cells on each of twelve rows starting at $415D. The destination advances by 40 bytes per row.
Decrement $2CFA. At one sample the joystick and request sound $81. At zero call the five-sprite update and reset the countdown to one.
Set $2D23 to $FF, increment the phase at $2CF8 and invert $2CF9 on odd phases. Call $28F7 for indices 4 through 0.
Use $0D to select the sprite. Check the frame toggle bytes, adjust the frame pointer and apply the position update under the current range flags and displacement tables.
Initialize five coordinate pairs from $2CFB, copy initial motion flags and frame pointers, set the sprite colours and clear the encounter flags before setting high X for sprites 0 and 1.
Decrement $2CFA. At expiry reload two and call the updater at $29C5 for sprites 1 and 0.
Use $0D to locate the pointer and its VIC Y register. Change the frame between adjacent pointers near $B7 and adjust the sprite Y to match the changed pose.
Load the coordinates and pointers for four sprites, reset their animation fields and initialize their divider from the four seeds at $3193. Enable all sprites and clear expansion for the first four.
Select frames $B7/$B8 for sprites 0 and 1, install their first position group and clear both pose flags before enabling the new sprite set.
Compute 90 times A, add $3200 and copy that pose record to $44–$9D after synchronizing to the lower half of the raster.
Use A to index an 18-byte record at $305B. Copy positions for sprites 4–7, four colors and four pointers, then combine the high nibble expansion masks with the existing low nibbles.
Select the next raster target at $2B70 and its line from $99. Apply the first band position, pointer, colour and expansion values to sprites 5–7.
Select the third raster update and line from $9A. Load the second band sprite positions from $50–$55, colours and pointers before restoring the expansion set.
Apply the third band sprite record and select the next handler at $2BEA on the line in $9B.
Select the fifth raster band using line $9C, then apply sprite coordinates from $68–$6D and pointer values from $71–$73.
Install $2C69 for the next interrupt at the compare line saved in $9D. Apply the fifth group of position, palette and shape values to sprites 5–7.
Select the first handler at $2B2E and the compare line in $98. Apply the sixth pose group to sprites 5–7 and service the common sound update before returning.
Use the resident sound update and jump into the shared IRQ epilogue.
Wait through the common raster synchronization and set the IRQ target to the Skull Hallway handler at $2B2E.

Read active-high joystick masks and return the sample on an exact match to A. No movement and samples suppressed during cooldown return $FF. An incorrect nonzero mask also queues sound $89 and starts the 20-call cooldown.
Four registers for sprites 0 and 1. The setup at $2A86 copies them to $D000–$D003.
Four alternate sprite 0 and sprite 1 position bytes installed by $2A1C.
Four VIC coordinates installed in the scripted state at $261D.
The second scripted position group, read at $2678.
The third scripted position group, read at $2702.
One state byte per animation slot, indexed by $29EF and initialized together at $2A14 and $2A17.
Action lockout loaded with $14 at $2CD6 and tested by the exact-mask input matcher.
Two bytes read by the timed frame update at $28FC and $2902.
Countdown used at $29AE. Reload with two before stepping timed poses.
Ten position bytes copied to sprites 0–4 by $296F.
Five per-sprite X adjustments indexed by $2936.
Five initial values copied by $297A to the movement fields at $2D0F.
Five values added or subtracted by $2955 and $2963 during the movement update.
Five initial bytes copied to their companion state at $2D19.
Five state values initialized from the seed table at $2D14.
Five frame pointers loaded at $298B and installed at $43F8.

Six initial zero bytes for the five-sprite sequence. The update writes the leading flag at $28D7, compares Y against the limit at $2D24 and uses $2D25 and $2D28 for its timed colour update. The shared delay at $27F9 uses $2D26.
Six rows of three screen codes for selector 0 of the patch copy at $283E.
Nine rows of four screen codes for selector 1 of the patch copy.
Three rows of four screen codes for selector 2 of the patch copy.
Character patch record addressed by four consecutive entries of the source pointer table. The adjoining records begin at $2D5F and $2D8F.
Nine rows of four screen codes copied with selector 7.
Nine rows of four screen codes copied with selector 8.
Nine rows of four screen codes copied with selector 9.
Ten little-endian source pointers indexed by twice the patch selector in $283E.
Ten screen destination words. The renderer derives the colour RAM destination by adding $98 to the high byte.
Eight coordinate values selected by the first scripted position loop at $1F79.
Eight VIC coordinate values selected by the next scripted position loop at $2155.
Successive coordinate records selected by the scripted position loops at $226E, $22A6 and $22EF.
The coordinate records read by the later scripted position loops at $23C1, $23F9 and $2442.
Ten source addresses for the six coordinate bytes installed by $20BC.
Ten source addresses for the three sprite pointers installed by $20C6.
Ten six-byte position records for sprites 1–3. Each holds the low X and Y register bytes in VIC order.
Ten three-byte records loaded into the frame pointer slots starting at $43F9.
Ten values indexed by the overlay selector and merged into the three vertical-expansion bits for sprites 1–3.
Nineteen little-endian source pointers indexed by twice the shape selector in the sprite 0 builder at $20CF.
Nineteen low-X and Y pairs selected for sprite 0 by the shape selector.
One sprite 0 horizontal expansion bit per shape selector, merged into $D01D.
One sprite 0 vertical expansion bit per shape selector, merged into $D017.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 35 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 29 bytes through $2F6A are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 39 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 25 bytes through $2F83 are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 35 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 29 bytes through $2FA0 are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 60 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 4 bytes through $2FA4 are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 23 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 41 bytes through $2FCD are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 45 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 19 bytes through $2FE0 are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 37 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 27 bytes through $2FFB are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 57 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 7 bytes through $3002 are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 15 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 49 bytes through $3033 are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Packed sprite 0 frame. The initial count 24 selects the leading zero bytes. The following 40 bytes through $305B are literals for the frame at $6A40.
Sixteen 18-byte records selected by $2ADC. Each gives positions, colours and frame pointers for sprites 4–7 and the two expansion masks.
Eight position values copied into the first four sprite coordinate pairs at $2A31.
Four initial frame pointers installed by the setup at $2A41.
Four fields set to zero during sprite initialization. The frame update reads them by slot.
Four slots initialized to five before the final sprite sequence.
Four countdowns used by $2782. At each expiry the slot reloads to two.
Four initialization values copied to the sprite divider fields at $318F.
Four pairs loaded as VIC position bytes by the scripted loop at $252C.
Four alternate pairs of VIC position bytes read by $2599.
Displacement applied with opposite signs by the sprite frame update at $27B8 and $27E9.
The first raster handler clears this byte at $2B30 before installing the next handler at $2B70.
This scene record ends with the eleven byte marker copied by the unpacker at $0DDE.
The first page of the screen matrix for the background in VIC bank $4000. Its character codes index the scene colour lookup when the display is initialized.
Screen matrix offsets $100–$1FF. The VIC reads these as character codes and the palette routine processes a page at a time.
Screen matrix offsets $200–$2FF. The screen maps into the glyph data at $7800.
The last page of the screen matrix, including the hardware sprite pointers at $43F8–$43FF.
The first two rendered hallway sprite fragments immediately before the pair loaded into sprites 5 and 6.
Two consecutive 64-byte sprite records selected by hardware sprites 5 and 6 in the Skull Hallway play capture, using VIC pointers $12 and $13.
Sixteen adjacent sprite frames. Rendering the uncompressed records shows torso, head and leg fragments in different poses for the hallway animation.
The next sixteen sprite pieces, including extended arms and rounded head fragments.
A run of 16 sprite pieces with bent or straight legs and the companion upper-body pieces.
Sprite pieces include extended steps in the early records and small torso and head fragments in the later records.
Mid-range hallway animation shapes. The code selects pointer $63 for sprite 1 at $225E.
Adjacent body and face sprite pieces. The animation sets pointer $6F at $2296 and $68 at $229E.
Sixteen 64-byte sprite slots including the fragment selected by the immediate pointer $74 at $22DD.
Sprite slots including the mask pointed to by sprite 1 when $22D7 writes $85. Several consecutive images show falling body poses.
Rendered shapes include angled legs and drifting silhouettes in 64-byte steps.
A run of limb silhouettes, including the $A9 sprite selected by the routine at $20CF.
The sixteen shapes around pointer $C0, which is selected for sprite 3 at $22E7.
The final compact bank of individual sprite pieces begins at pointer $C4 and includes legs, a torso and a moving overhead figure.
Two 64-byte sprite shapes at pointers $CE and $CF. The frames match the same slots in the Tentacle Room graphics bank.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $7400–$75FF to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
Two 64-byte sprites at VIC pointers $D8 and $D9. The initial pointer table at $3183 selects these shapes for the final sprite sequence.
Two blank 64-byte VIC sprite slots between the final pose sprites at pointers $D8–$D9 and the palette lookup page at $7700.
Table indexed by the screen cell at $4000–$43FF during initialization. Each entry supplies the colour RAM nibble for that cell.
The scene character glyph store for VIC bank $4000 and character-base bits 3–1 of $D018 set to 7. A character occupies eight consecutive bytes.
The top half of this scene set, from character code $80. The eight-byte glyph slots are used for the scene-specific objects and screen details.
The LA bytes at $BD21–$BD21 follow the last source token required by the scene picture decoder and precede the repeated disk fill.
Repeated $02 bytes at $BD22–$BF0F, after the input consumed by the scene picture decode.
